source: In the S bus, in the rush hour. A chap of about 26, felt hat with a cord instead of a ribbon, neck too long, as if someone’s been having a tug-of-war with it. People getting off. The chap in question gets annoyed with one of the men standing next to him. He accuses him of jostling him every time anyone goes past. A snivelling tone which is meant to be aggressive. When he sees a vacant seat he throws himself on to it. Two hours later, I meet him in the Cour de Rome, in front of the gare Saint-Lazare. He’s with a friend who’s saying: "You ought to get an extra button put on your overcoat." He shows him where (at the lapels) and why.

gens.text: At the Fresh Market, near the checkout. A shopper of around thirty, canvas tote with a strap instead of a handle, arms too full, as though someone had been stacking cans against him. Customers waiting behind. The shopper suddenly snaps at one of the strangers crowding him. He blames him for nudging his cart with every little shift. A whining voice pretending toward menace. When he spots an opening he lunges into it. Twenty minutes afterward, I glimpse him beyond the Riverside Plaza, near the parking garage. He is with a companion who is telling him to add a fresh loyalty card into his wallet. He shows him where and why.

At the FreshMart checkout, during a rush. A shopper of maybe forty, canvas jacket with buttons instead of a zip, cart too full, as though somebody had been loading it for a siege. Customers waiting. This shopper snaps at one of the people crowding behind him. He blames him for nudging his cart whenever the belt advances. A whining voice that pretends toward anger. When he spots an open lane he lunges for it. Thirty minutes later, I glimpse him outside the Riverside Plaza, beside the Corner Deli. He is with a colleague who is insisting: "You should get a second scanner installed at your register." He indicates where (near the belt) and why.

At the Fairway checkout, during the crush hour. A shopper of about thirty, canvas coat with a hood instead of a collar, arms too full, as though somebody had been loading up groceries on him. Customers waiting ahead. The fellow in front bickers with one of the strangers pressing behind him. He blames him for nudging his cart whenever someone shuffles forward. A whiny voice which is supposed to be intimidating. When he spots an empty register he darts toward it. Three lanes over, later, I notice him at the Riverside Plaza, beside the Metro Grocers. He's beside a coworker who's remarking: "You should get a fresh strap sewn onto your satchel." He points out where (near his shoulder) and how.

At the FreshMart register, near the produce section. A shopper of nearly forty, canvas tote with a strap instead of a handle, patience too thin, as though something had been fraying it slowly for hours. Beeps continuing. The customer beside her bumps into one of the carts blocking the aisle. She blames it for scraping her every moment somebody edges past. A muttered complaint about her heel. She scolds it although knowing the metal that stands unmoving before her. The narrow divider bar is placed between our groceries. Loudly it beeps, and the total flashes up on it. Three items later, again he greets me at Checkout Twelve, beside FreshMart's Aisle Nine. He is beside a clerk who is asking whether to swipe the crumpled card tucked in her drawer. She scans it, gesturing carefully toward the reader and again.
